title: Twelve yards of nerve
text: No sporting act is simpler {{1}} striking a stationary ball from twelve yards, and {{2}} is stranger than the psychology that surrounds it. {{3}} is the walk from the centre circle to the penalty spot that gives a player time to think, and thinking was never meant to be part of the job. Goalkeepers {{4}} studied opponents' habits know that most players decide where to shoot only {{5}} they begin the walk, which is why psychologists teach strikers to choose a corner early and commit. {{6}} the research shows, however, is that goalkeepers who stay upright for longer save {{7}} penalties than those who dive at the first twitch. Twelve yards may be the shortest distance in sport, {{8}} it contains a whole seminar on nerve.

gaps.hint: pronoun: and ___ is stranger than the psychology
gaps.explanation: 'Nothing is stranger than…' — the emphatic negative comparison.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ is the walk that gives time
gaps.explanation: The cleft structure emphasises the walk.
Present perfect participle clause with a plural subject: have studied.

gaps.hint: time word: only ___ they begin the walk
pronoun: ___ the research shows is that
gaps.explanation: Fused relative subject of the pseudo-cleft.

gaps.hint: conjunction: the shortest distance, ___ it contains a seminar
gaps.explanation: Contrast between small distance and big lesson: but.
